reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents couponing content showing a reported $5 gift card being used to reduce household purchase costs, alongside Lowe's receipts documenting discounts and totals. The text instruction to send "SPRING" to 78133 is an external offer whose validity remains unverified, but the described material frames the video as an ordinary promotional couponing demonstration rather than a deceptive financial scheme.

So, take advantage of it, send it a message. to number 78133. with the word SPRING. and take advantage of the gift card.

opening.argument: Judge, the offer is structured as a reward in exchange for a simple action. The title promises a free Lowe's gift card and gives the text-message instruction; the speaker raises the possible value to $500. That pairing matters more than the household products: viewers are being asked to contact a number to claim an easy reward. The speaker's reported $5 discount does not establish that the promised offer is available to viewers who follow the instruction.

citations.quote: Lowe's Gift Card Free !! | Send text to 78133 with the word spring | luck
it can be a $5 gift card up to $500. it depends on the luck of one.
he sent me a $5 gift card to my phone number.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to a reported discount, but a discount on the speaker's purchase does not verify the offer a viewer is asked to pursue. The invitation is explicit: text the number and take advantage of the gift card. Receipts can support the reported purchase while leaving that viewer-facing promise unverified.

citations.quote: So, take advantage of it, send it a message. to number 78133. with the word SPRING. and take advantage of the gift card.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The message instruction is real, but a promise-action pair alone does not show deception. The speaker describes receiving a $5 gift card and applying a $5 discount to a purchase; the displayed receipt also shows that discount. Nothing cited by the prosecution shows that texting the number misleads viewers or prevents them from receiving the described promotion.

opening.argument: The concerning combination is the size of the possible reward, the ease of entry, and the speaker's personal success story. A gift card said to reach $500 depends only on luck, while the stated action is simply texting a keyword. The speaker then presents a $5 benefit on a purchase. That small, concrete example can make the much larger possibility sound credible, even though it does not substantiate the $500 outcome or establish what a viewer will receive.

citations.quote: it can be a $5 gift card up to $500. it depends on the luck of one.
all they have to do is text the number 78133. with the word SPRING.
they discounted the 5 of the card they sent me

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's receipts address the modest discount, not the claim most likely to draw attention: a chance at up to $500. The speaker distinguishes her own $5 result from that larger possibility. Evidence of one discount therefore cannot verify the advertised range or the offer's terms for other participants.

citations.quote: it can be a $5 gift card up to $500. it depends on the luck of one.
he sent me a $5 gift card to my phone number.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker explicitly qualifies the upper amount as dependent on luck and reports receiving $5 herself. The purchase discussion and displayed receipts are consistent with that reported smaller benefit. No cited evidence contradicts the stated range or shows that the text-message offer is deceptive; an unverified maximum is not, by itself, proof of a scam.

citations.quote: it can be a $5 gift card up to $500. it depends on the luck of one.
he sent me a $5 gift card to my phone number.

opening.argument: The couponing demonstration also functions as a pitch. The title leads with a free gift card and the precise text instruction, and the description repeats that instruction before telling viewers to present a barcode to the cashier. The product prices and receipts make the pitch feel like practical shopping advice, but the requested viewer action remains contacting the number to pursue the reward. The purchase evidence does not establish the conditions of that offer for anyone following the video.

let me show you. the receipt here is 8.98 the gift and they discounted the 5 of the gift that they sent me to 3.98.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this couponing does not answer what the couponing presentation asks viewers to do. The speaker moves from showing a discounted purchase to urging viewers to message 78133 for a gift card. The receipts support her account of a discount; they do not establish that this instruction is a reliable route to the promised reward.

citations.quote: So, take advantage of it, send it a message. to number 78133. with the word SPRING. and take advantage of the gift card.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A couponing video can recommend a promotion without becoming a scam. Here the speaker describes specific purchases and how a $5 discount affected their totals, and the sampled receipts show corresponding discounts. The prosecution identifies a promotional purpose but supplies no evidence that the message instruction or reported reward is false.
